title: Staircase attention kernels, prefetcher, and KV slab allocator - notes
content:
Context and goal:

This is an exploratory note collecting ideas for a low-latency, high-throughput attention kernel variant that plays nicely with a paged KV cache. The motivating constraints: 1) tail latency SLO of 50ms p95 for short-to-medium sequences (<= 512 tokens) on A100/RTX-class hardware, 2) high aggregate throughput for batched streaming inference, 3) efficient memory usage for multi-tenant paged KV.

High-level idea ("staircase" pattern):
- Break attention into a set of staggered tiles (stair-steps) across sequence length and head dims so we can start producing partial outputs earlier while prefetching downstream KV pages.
- Combine warp-cooperative FlashAttention micro-tiles with an asynchronous prefetch scheduler that pulls KV pages into slab-allocated pinned host buffers and then into GPU shared memory/regs where possible.
- Use a KV "slab allocator" to reduce fragmentation of paged KV, enabling fast eviction/compaction and per-slab prefetch hints.

Design components (notes):

1) Staircase tiling for latency-sensitive workloads
- Tile layout: along sequence dimension S split into tiles of Ts (e.g. 32/64), but we offset the start of each head-group tile by delta so head-groups can process in staggered order. This produces a steady stream of completed token outputs without waiting for full prefix.
- Advantage: first-token latency reduced because we compute partial attention for early heads/tiles and emit partials while later tiles are prefetched.
- Tradeoffs: more kernels launches; must amortize launch overhead via batched micro-tiles and persistent kernel where possible.

2) Warp-cooperative FlashAttention variant
- Base on FlashAttention v2 patterns but tailor for micro-tiles: use warp-level reductions for QK dot products and fused softmax where numerical stability preserved using block-wise max and exp sums.
- Prefer half2/float16 where model tested safe; expose mixed-precision toggles for critical layers.
- Replace expensive global memory scatter/gather with cooperative loads into shared memory arranged to minimize bank conflicts. Use padding to avoid 32-bit bank aliasing when reading KV when head dim % 32 != 0.

3) Prefetch scheduler (async)
- Prefetch stages: 1) issue read-ahead signals from runtime (based on request token offsets) -> 2) coordinator schedules page fetches from disk/host cache to pinned host buffers (cudaHostAlloc) using async IO -> 3) cudaMemcpyAsync peer-to-peer into device buffers, then signal CUDA events for kernel consumption.
- Heuristics: prefetch horizon proportional to expected per-request token consumption and head-group start staggering. Conservative default: 2*Ts ahead for medium tails, 6*Ts for heavy streaming.
- Backpressure: if device memory pressure high, prefetcher reduces horizon; maintain a per-stream token budget.

4) KV slab allocator and paging policy
- Slab units: fixed-size slabs (e.g., 8MB, tunable) holding contiguous KV ranges for multiple keys. Slabs minimize metadata and speed up eviction compaction.
- Hotness tracking: per-slab LRU with per-key access counters; use a tiny aging counter that decays every N requests to avoid runaway hot keys.
- Compaction: when slab fragmentation > threshold, sweep to compact live KV into new slab and free old slabs. Compaction is backgrounded and can be paused under memory pressure.
- Page alignment: align slab pages with GPU page size for efficient cudaMemcpy ranges and to exploit HW page granularity for unified memory flows.

5) Kernel-level fusion opportunities
- Fused KV load + attention compute: fuse the path that loads KV tile from device memory into registers/shared memory directly into the attention compute kernel (no extra store). For this, prefetch steps must have ensured data ready in device buffer or we must fall back to an alternate path with explicit load.
- Fused quant-dequant path: support on-the-fly dequantization for 4-bit/8-bit KV where registers receive dequantized float16 values as part of the load loop. This reduces memory bandwidth but increases ALU overhead; evaluate on local perf bench.
- Fusion caveat: fused kernels increase register pressure and can reduce occupancy; use profiling to choose when to fuse vs two-step copy+compute.

6) Asynchronous and persistent kernels
- Prefer persistent threadblock kernels for long-lived streams to avoid kernel launch overhead; these kernels spin on work-queues and respond to events indicating pages/tiles ready.
- Use CUDA events and lightweight spin-wait with backoff for signaling. Carefully design to avoid wasting SM cycles—sleep via cooperative groups or use stream callback model when available.

7) Precision and quantization notes
- For 4-bit KV storage (GPTQ-ish), store scales per-slab or per-block, not per-key when possible to keep metadata small. Evaluate MSE vs per-key scales.
- Provide runtime switch to do compute in fp16 or bf16 for final accumulation; maintain reference fp32 path for testing.

8) Memory layout and bank-aware packing
- Layout recommendation: K/V contiguous per head, with head-major ordering inside slab to allow contiguous lanewise reads for warp loads.
- Insert stride padding to avoid shared-memory bank conflicts where head_dim%32 small values cause mod aliasing.
- For small heads use lane-swizzled layout to make vector loads coalesced.

9) Metrics and microbench plan
- Per-kernel metrics: achieved occupancy, regs per thread, shared memory used, memory bandwidth (GB/s), L2 hit rate, global load/store efficiency.
- High-level SLO tests: p50/p95 latency for sequences [16, 64, 256, 512] with batch sizes [1,4,8]; throughput for long-running streams (sustained tokens/s).
- Add synthetic microbench for prefetch latency: measure end-to-end time from host prefetch request -> GPU-ready event under different slab sizes and host pinned buffer counts.

10) Safety nets, graceful fallback
- Fallback path: if slab not resident or prefetch missed, fall back to slower but robust path: normal non-fused kernel that does direct loads from global device memory with explicit boundary checks.
- Degrade gracefully by increasing prefetch horizon in the short-term when repeated misses observed.

Open questions / research items:
- Optimal slab size across different head_dim and sequence distributions — empirical tuning required. Start with 8MB/16MB experiments.
- Best heuristic for staggering offsets (delta) across head-groups. Is simple round-robin enough or a latency-weighted greedy ordering better?
- How to integrate with Dedicated mode where per-tenant isolation requires hard memory caps? Slab eviction policies must respect tenant quotas.
- Effect of fused dequant path on temperature/ALU bottleneck for A100; quantify with per-SM utilization traces.

Action items:
- Proto: implement a minimal persistent kernel that consumes prepopulated device buffers and performs stair-step micro-tiles for a single transformer layer. (Owner: Marcus)
- Bench: microbench prefetcher latency with slab sizes {4MB,8MB,16MB} and pinned buffers {2,4,8}. (Owner: Diego)
- Simulation: run traffic replay on paged-KV simulator with staggered tiling enabled to measure p95 improvements vs baseline. (Owner: Priya)
- Doc: consolidate perf knobs into a single runtime config blob (prefetch_horizon, slab_size, fusion_mode, fallback_threshold). (Owner: Aisha)

Notes to self / rough experiments to try quickly:
- Try half2 loads in flash-attn inner loop and compare against vectorized fp16 loads; check throughput difference at head_dim=64 vs head_dim=128.
- Test small persistent-kernel sleep strategies: cudaStreamWaitEvent vs tiny kernel loop with __nanosleep-like backoff (or cooperative groups).
- Verify that per-slab scale caching for 4-bit quantization doesn't blow up model quality; log dequant residuals per-slab to spot drift.

References and related work:
- FlashAttention (paper + impl) - use for micro-tile reduction / fused softmax patterns.
- Kernel fusion patterns in 1) persistent kernels and 2) pipelined GEMM-launch fusion docs.

Unresolved implementation constraints:
- Avoid overfitting to a single GPU family; parametrize tile sizes and occupancy targets per-cuda-capability.
- Keep ABI between runtime and kernel simple: pass small descriptor struct (address, stride, slab_id, scale_ptr) but runtime will manage indirection.

Endnote: these are working notes. The goal is a pragmatic set of experiments that can be completed within 2–4 sprints and yield measurable latency improvements for our short-sequence p95s without regressing throughput for large-batch inference.

-- Priya
